name: Mach Travel Solutions Ltd
title: Mach Travel Solutions Ltd - 544248 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue INR144.33 cr (+538% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell to 6.09% from 7.17%, management admits markup cuts for aggressive market share and working-capital strain requires bank OD.

summary.headline: Mach Travel Q1 FY27 revenue rose 538% YoY to INR144.33 crore, with EBITDA margin compressing to 6.09% from 7.17%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR144.33 crore versus INR22.62 crore a year ago and INR83.25 crore in Q4 FY26, with GMV of about INR252 crore disclosed for the first time. EBITDA rose to INR8.92 crore and PAT to INR6.17 crore, but margins were lower YoY, which management attributed to investment in new verticals, hiring and technology. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR500-plus crore and said it is working on bank overdraft lines because of working capital pressure from payment cycles. Much of the quarter's growth came from a few large government and MICE programmes, and several answers were vague or deferred.

financial_highlights.change: +538% YoY vs INR22.62 crore; +73% QoQ vs INR83.25 crore
+437% YoY vs INR1.66 crore; QoQ up from INR3.81 crore
+307% YoY vs INR1.52 crore; QoQ up from INR1.8 crore
Management described company as debt free

segments.name: MICE (core)
segments.commentary: Management estimated MICE at about INR100 crore of Q1 revenue in one answer, then said INR50-60 crore in another, so the split is unclear. Oceania programmes worth about INR32 crore were completed, covering 950-1,000 delegates.

segments.name: Corporate travel
segments.commentary: Launched in April 2026 with more than 100 corporate clients signed; management put it at about 10-15% of revenue. Billing cycles run 1st-15th payable on the 20th and 16th-30th payable on the 6th-7th of the next month.

segments.name: Government and institutional (Punjab Yatra)
segments.commentary: Punjab Yatra contract worth about INR92 crore covering 1.85 lakh yatris, at about INR4,950 per person for a 2-night, 3-day trip. Management said about 15% of Q1 revenue came from it; about 1.15 lakh travelled to date and the contract runs to about November.

segments.name: IRCTC
segments.commentary: Empanelled as one of four or five A-listed vendors, with a first order of about INR75 lakh to INR1 crore. Empanelment term was stated as two years, extendable, but the executive director was not certain.

segments.name: B2B and B2C OTA / leisure
segments.commentary: B2B tool lets smaller travel agents book tickets. B2C app Machtravel.com is in testing and its launch was pushed from late August to September 2026. Leisure was described as doing very well, with no figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of around INR500-plus crore, reiterated and described as an average-based figure; management expects to surpass it.
Management said quarter-on-quarter growth will not be substantial because October-December is a festival and Christmas lull for corporate travel; Q2 is seasonally heavier than Q1 overall.
Management would not commit to a date for EBITDA margins returning to the roughly 10% level mentioned by an analyst, and would not say margins will be under pressure in Q2.
Markups may be compressed in aggressive pursuit of business, but management said the company will not burn money.
Next milestones named: INR500 crore, then INR1,000 crore revenue, B2C app launch in September, a possible main board move within 12 months, and new southern offices.
capex_capacity: Operating presence expanded to Noida, New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Bhubaneshwar and Ahmedabad; more southern offices planned.
Investment in technology, talent and offices over the past year is cited as the cause of lower margins; no quantified capex figure was given.
Corporate self-booking tool (SBT) covers booking, approval, ticketing, invoicing and reporting; management said it uses the same technology as large players.
Captive audience of about 1.25 lakh travellers a year is to be moved onto the B2C portal and app.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the growth to the transition beyond MICE into corporate, B2B, leisure, government and B2C, and said the policies were implemented from 1 April 2026.
TTV (total ticketed volume) was about INR259-260 crore versus about INR143 crore in revenue; the call did not reconcile TTV with GMV of INR252 crore.
Management said pricing on the B2C app is at par with large B2C players.
Punjab Yatra daily flows are about 1,100 travellers out and 1,100 back, with about 3,300-3,500 people handled at any one time.
Management said it is not clear whether the Punjab yatra will be repeated; three other Punjab yatra programmes were not won. Management is in talks with other state governments.

qa_highlights.question: How did revenue grow from INR22 crore to INR140-plus crore, and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company spent about 1.5 years building new teams and technology and implemented the policies from April 2026. Revenue now comes from MICE, corporate, leisure, government and B2B; TTV was about INR259-260 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be managed to support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is debt free with about INR3 crore of debt, but payment-cycle issues have created a working capital need. It is working toward bank overdraft facilities and will update the market if availed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between core MICE and the new verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was unsure of the exact split. It said about INR50-60 crore came from MICE in one answer and about INR100 crore in another, with corporate at 10-15% and the Punjab Yatra at about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margins recover to about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no firm date. It said margins will improve as business scales, buying power rises and markups increase, but that it will be aggressive in the market and may give up some markup.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500 crore guidance conservative given Q1 was about 29-30% of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is an annual average and cited seasonality. It said it hopes to surpass INR500 crore, but expects no substantial quarter-on-quarter growth in Q2 and Q3 because of festival periods.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Punjab Yatra contract repeatable, and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract is for 1.85 lakh yatris at about INR4,950 per person and runs to about November. Payment is about 7 days after travel, roughly 15 days in total. It was unsure whether the programme would be repeated.

risks_watch: Working capital strain: management said payment cycles have created a working capital need and the company is working toward bank overdraft lines; watch for the OD sanction, size and terms.

Revenue concentration: Punjab Yatra (about INR92 crore contract, roughly 15% of Q1 revenue) runs to about November, and management was unsure whether it will be repeated after three other Punjab yatra bids were lost.
Margin trajectory: EBITDA margin was 6.09% vs 7.17% a year ago, and management gave no date for recovery and said it will give up some markup to win business.
Unclear revenue split: management gave MICE as INR50-60 crore in one answer and about INR100 crore in another; TTV of about INR259-260 crore was not reconciled with GMV of about INR252 crore.

Q2 and Q3 guidance: management said quarter-on-quarter growth will not be substantial due to festival and Christmas seasonality; watch Q2 numbers against the INR500-plus crore FY27 target and the B2C app launch slipping to September 2026.
key_quotes: Currently we are a debt free company with just about INR3 crores of debt.
there is a thought of raising some money from banks in terms of OD. Currently, yes, there are issues with the payment cycle.
I would not say that the margins would have pressure, but try and understand that we are running a profitable company and we've been doing it for last 22 years. We do not want to burn money
I am not sure whether this will be repeated or not. But here our business would go on till November, and we are likely to achieve this number by November.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the growth narrative and the INR500-plus crore FY27 target, but evasive on specifics: the MICE/corporate revenue split, IRCTC empanelment term, the business it won, margin recovery timing and Punjab yatra repeatability were all deferred or left unquantified. Cautious on working capital, where it acknowledged payment-cycle pressure and a need for bank overdraft lines.

adds.what: New southern offices planned (no count or capex given)
B2C app Machtravel.com launch (pushed to September 2026)

growth.why: FY27 revenue target of around INR500-plus crore was reiterated (not raised), with partial backing from the Punjab Yatra contract (~INR92 crore, ~15% of Q1 revenue), corporate travel (100+ clients) and IRCTC empanelment, but management guided QoQ growth to be muted in Q2 and gave no quantified capacity additions.
